main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large stepped thatch roof slope (rows 0-36) over a timber front wall with a plank door and a shuttered window (rows 37-63)
top_band: The roof slope fills rows 1-35, drawn as stacked horizontal thatch courses in light gold (L 156-214) with a lighter ridge at row 1. A lighter eave band at rows 34-36 closes it, and a dark shadow row sits at rows 37-38.
evidence: The roof is a big, widening slope seen from above. It has a ridge highlight at the top and an overhanging eave at rows 34-36 with a dark shadow under it at rows 37-38, so it reads as a roof surface and not a flat hat. Below it is a separate vertical wall face. The door has a dark frame and the window has a dark inset opening and sill. No receding side faces. The roof-over-wall structure matches the Beodeul house references, so it passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about six tones (#5e4218 up to #f0d888) with per-course notches and speckle. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels) and not a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. The planks and door have grain and hinge details. Density is lower than the references: 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 29 distinct colours against 66 and 185. Much of that gap comes from the locked, narrow palette and the small piece, so the craft still sits acceptably next to the references.
